description: I am a passionate student interested in space exploration, science, technology, and creative problem-solving. I enjoy learning new things and developing innovative ideas. My interests include computer science, graphic design, research, and artificial intelligence. I aim to create a meaningful and creative solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge while exploring new skills and technologies.​
summary:
RED PLANET RESCUE is an interactive educational Mars outpost resource-management simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Players take the role of a Mars outpost commander and make decisions across five mission scenarios: solar storms, water recycling issues, oxygen system warnings, food supply challenges, and radiation alerts. They manage five essential resources: Water, Oxygen, Power, Food, and Radiation Protection.

The simulator helps users explore the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars through interactive decisions and a final mission performance report. It incorporates NASA resources and space-related data for educational context. Resource levels and scores are illustrative game mechanics, not real NASA measurements or safety ratings.

The project aims to make space exploration concepts engaging, accessible, and educational.
details:
RED PLANET RESCUE is an interactive educational Mars outpost resource-management simulator. It allows users to experience the role of a Mars outpost commander and make decisions to keep a crew and their outpost functioning.

The simulator includes five mission scenarios: solar storms, water recycling problems, oxygen system warnings, food supply challenges, and radiation alerts. Players manage five essential resources: Water, Oxygen, Power, Food, and Radiation Protection. Their decisions affect resource levels and the final mission performance report.

The project aims to make the challenges of human exploration and long-term survival on Mars engaging and accessible to students. It encourages decision-making, resource management, and learning about space exploration.

The website was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code and published through GitHub Pages. NASA resources were used for educational and space-data context. The resource levels and scores are illustrative game mechanics, not real NASA measurements or safety ratings.

ChatGPT was used to assist with code development and text refinement. The project concept, design choices, implementation, and testing were directed and reviewed by the student developer.
